gallery.filename: Hohokam Sacaton red-on-buff plate, crica 950-1150 AD.JPG
gallery.title: File:Hohokam Sacaton red-on-buff plate, crica 950-1150 AD.JPG
gallery.artist: Peter D. Tillman from USA
gallery.credit: Hohokam Sacaton red-on-buff plate, crica 950-1150 AD
gallery.source: Hohokam Sacaton red-on-buff plate, crica 950-1150 AD
gallery.description: A classic Hohokam design on a large plate. Labelled "SRP Heritage", which I think means it was recovered somewhere on the SRP's extensive network of power lines  that serve PHX from the upstream SRP dams. About 14 " diameter, by memory. The design motif is likely an unfolding Sacred Datura bud, a widespread interest among the ancient Hohokam and other cultural groups.

gallery.filename: Sacaton red on buff pot, ca. 950-1150, Pueblo Grande museum.JPG
gallery.title: File:Sacaton red on buff pot, ca. 950-1150, Pueblo Grande museum.JPG
gallery.artist: Peter D. Tillman from USA
gallery.description:
A classic "Gila shoulder" pot, a favorite of these folks, and of collectors ever since. This one seems to have been recovered intact from the PG ruins.
Pueblo Grande museum was established in  1929, with the hiring of Odd Halseth as Americas' first City Archaeologist. Per the volunteer on duty, Mr. Halseth built the first adobe museum buildings for a cash outlay of around $20.00 (for nails & hardware), as the city had no extra cash for such things in the Great Depression. In this 70th anniversary year, park staff have some of their favorite art and artifacts on display.

The repeated "W" motif is simply coincidence (see date), but intriguing....
